entries.name: A2UI
entries.use_for: Let agents describe rich UIs as safe JSON that your own app renders with trusted components.
entries.why: A declarative format, not code: agents can only request components from a catalog your app approves.
entries.summary: A2UI (Agent-to-User Interface) is an open format and set of renderers for agent-generated UIs. The agent sends a flat list of components plus a data model, and the client maps them to native widgets. The format is easy for an LLM to build up step by step.
entries.best_for: Agents that need forms, dashboards or cards in a chat UI without running model-written code.
entries.not_for: Stable production use yet. The README calls it an early-stage public preview, and the specification is still changing.

entries.name: Angular Material & CDK
entries.use_for: Official Material Design components and the CDK behaviour primitives for Angular
entries.why: The standard component library for Angular apps, maintained by the Angular team; the CDK is the base for many other kits.
entries.summary: Angular team's component packages: Angular Material (Material Design components), the CDK for building custom components, headless ARIA directives (@angular/aria), Google Maps and more.
entries.best_for: Angular apps wanting official Material components or the CDK primitives (overlay, a11y, drag-drop, virtual scroll) to build a custom design system.
entries.not_for: Angular only. Material's look is hard to restyle away from Material Design, and it lacks the data-heavy enterprise widgets of suites like PrimeNG.

entries.name: Animal-Island-UI
entries.use_for: Add a cozy, cute island-themed component set to a React app.
entries.why: Original, playful visual style with custom icons and animations, in a lightweight TypeScript package.
entries.summary: A React and TypeScript component library with an island-style design language. You import components such as Button and Card plus a style file. A Vue version and an icon set are linked from the README.
entries.best_for: Playful, game-like or kids-friendly interfaces where a standard corporate design system feels wrong.
entries.not_for: Strong themed look. The README lists a small set of components, so check coverage for complex apps.

entries.name: Ant Design
entries.use_for: Build data-heavy enterprise React apps with a large, consistent component set.
entries.why: Very complete set (tables, forms, pickers) with strong i18n; widely used for admin and back-office apps.
entries.summary: Enterprise-focused React UI library and design language with a large set of components written in TypeScript, i18n for dozens of languages, and design resources and tooling.
entries.best_for: Admin dashboards, back-office tools and data-heavy enterprise React apps needing tables, forms and pickers quickly.
entries.not_for: React only with an opinionated visual style; bundle size and heavy customization can be a burden for lightweight or highly branded consumer sites.

entries.name: Ant Design Vue
entries.use_for: Enterprise-grade Ant Design components for Vue
entries.why: Vue implementation of Ant Design with tables, forms and data-heavy admin components.
entries.summary: Vue implementation of the Ant Design system, offering enterprise-style components for desktop apps and sharing Ant Design resources with the React version.
entries.best_for: Vue admin panels and data-heavy internal tools that want Ant Design's look and component set.
entries.not_for: Desktop-oriented and tied to Ant Design's visual language; check Vue 3 compatibility and release cadence versus Element Plus or Naive UI.

entries.name: assistant-ui
entries.use_for: React components for AI chat interfaces
entries.why: Composable, shadcn-style primitives for chat UIs with streaming, tool calls and attachments; works with AI SDK and LangGraph.
entries.summary: TypeScript/React library for AI chat interfaces with composable primitives (Thread, Message, Composer, ThreadList). Handles streaming, auto-scroll and retries, offers shadcn-style themes via CLI, and connects to Vercel AI SDK, LangGraph or custom runtimes.
entries.best_for: React or Next.js apps needing a ChatGPT-like UI on top of AI SDK, LangGraph or your own backend.
entries.not_for: React only and focused on chat UX; it is not an LLM backend or agent framework. Non-chat AI interfaces will need other components.

entries.name: Astryx
entries.use_for: Build React apps on a large, themeable design system with typed components and a CLI.
entries.why: Eight years of Meta use; no build plugin, and override styles with Tailwind or plain CSS.
entries.summary: A design system from Meta with 150+ accessible React components, theming through CSS custom properties, dark mode, templates and a CLI. Styles are authored in StyleX but consumers import pre-built CSS. A swizzle command ejects a component's source.
entries.best_for: React 19 teams that want a full component system they can restyle and, when needed, take ownership of the source.
entries.not_for: Non-React projects or React versions below 19. It is currently in beta.

entries.name: Base UI
entries.use_for: Build custom-styled React components on unstyled, accessible building blocks.
entries.why: From the Radix, Floating UI and MUI teams; a modern headless alternative with active development.
entries.summary: Unstyled, accessible React component library from the creators of Radix, Floating UI and Material UI. Provides headless building blocks you style yourself.
entries.best_for: Building a custom design system in React where accessibility is handled but styling is fully yours (CSS, Tailwind, CSS-in-JS).
entries.not_for: Provides no visual styling, so it is slower than a styled kit for quick prototypes. React only; the README gives little detail on component coverage.

entries.name: Blueprint
entries.use_for: React UI toolkit for complex, data-dense desktop-style web interfaces
entries.why: Battle-tested at Palantir for dense dashboards and tools; strong tables, trees and date pickers.
entries.summary: React UI toolkit for complex, data-dense desktop web interfaces, with components such as tables, trees, date pickers, selects and icons, organized as multiple packages.
entries.best_for: Desktop-style dashboards and tools with dense data views in modern browsers.
entries.not_for: Explicitly not mobile-first and React only. Its distinct visual identity may not suit consumer-facing or heavily branded products.

entries.name: boneyard
entries.use_for: Generate skeleton loading screens from your real UI instead of drawing placeholders by hand.
entries.why: A headless browser snapshots real layouts at several breakpoints and writes one shared .bones.json format.
entries.summary: boneyard captures your rendered components and produces skeletons. A CLI or Vite plugin visits the app, finds each Skeleton, and records layout. It works with React, Preact, Vue, Svelte 5, Angular and React Native.
entries.best_for: Apps that want skeleton screens matching the real layout without manual measuring.
entries.not_for: A build step that must see the real UI. Dynamic content may need a fixture. It only does skeleton placeholders.

entries.name: Canvas UI
entries.use_for: Wrap parts of a page in WebGL or WebGPU effects like liquid, glass and shatter while it stays interactive.
entries.why: Effects run over live DOM, with text still selectable and links clickable, and ship for six frameworks.
entries.summary: A library of 35 canvas effect components that use the experimental HTML-in-canvas API to redraw your live page. Each ships for React, Solid, Preact, Vue, Svelte and vanilla in WebGL and WebGPU builds. You copy source into your repo through a shadcn registry.
entries.best_for: Marketing sites and creative pages that want eye-catching shader effects without rebuilding the UI.
entries.not_for: Depends on an experimental browser API, with GPU overlay fallback elsewhere. The license is not clearly stated, so check before commercial use.

entries.name: Chakra UI
entries.use_for: Build accessible React UIs with style props and a themeable component system.
entries.why: Ergonomic style-prop API and solid accessibility; v3 is built on Ark UI and Panda-style tokens.
entries.summary: Accessible React component system with style props and themeable components. The README mentions Next.js RSC support and install via @chakra-ui/react with Emotion; docs exist for v0 to latest.
entries.best_for: React and Next.js projects wanting fast UI building with accessible, themeable components and style-prop ergonomics.
entries.not_for: React only and relies on Emotion CSS-in-JS runtime (per the install instructions). Major version migrations (v2 to v3) can be significant.

entries.name: Element Plus
entries.use_for: Build Vue 3 apps, especially admin panels, with a complete component set.
entries.why: The most used Vue 3 desktop component library with a large ecosystem of admin templates.
entries.summary: Vue 3 UI library written in TypeScript using the Composition API, with a broad component set and a migration path and tooling from Element UI.
entries.best_for: Vue 3 admin panels and desktop-oriented business apps, including projects migrating from Element UI.
entries.not_for: Vue 3 only and desktop-focused; not a headless or Tailwind-native kit. Customizing the default look takes theme overrides.

entries.name: Fluent UI
entries.use_for: Microsoft Fluent design system as React components and web components
entries.why: Powers Microsoft 365/Teams UIs; the choice for apps that should look native in the Microsoft ecosystem.
entries.summary: Microsoft's Fluent UI web repo with three projects: React v9 components, mature React v8, and Fluent Web Components. v9 and v8 can be mixed for gradual migration.
entries.best_for: Apps that should look and feel like Microsoft 365, Teams or Office, including add-ins, or that need Fluent web components.
entries.not_for: Strongly Microsoft-styled and tied to Fluent design. Multiple generations (v8, v9) create migration choices; not ideal for a distinctive brand look.

entries.name: Headless UI
entries.use_for: Unstyled, accessible React/Vue components designed to pair with Tailwind CSS
entries.why: From Tailwind Labs; the default headless kit for Tailwind projects (menus, dialogs, listboxes, comboboxes).
entries.stable_reason: v2 is feature-complete unstyled primitives maintained by Tailwind Labs; low churn by design
entries.summary: Set of completely unstyled, accessible UI components for React and Vue designed to pair with Tailwind CSS, such as menus, dialogs, listboxes and comboboxes.
entries.best_for: Tailwind projects needing accessible interactive primitives (dropdowns, modals, tabs, comboboxes) styled with utility classes.
entries.not_for: Limited to React and Vue and only offers a modest set of primitives; no tables, date pickers or full design system.

entries.name: HeroUI
entries.use_for: Build modern-looking React apps with Tailwind-based components (formerly NextUI).
entries.why: Polished default look on top of Tailwind and React Aria, popular with Next.js projects.
entries.summary: React component library (formerly NextUI) built on React Aria and Tailwind CSS v4 with a compound component API, no provider wrapper, React 19 support, and MCP server/llms.txt for AI assistants.
entries.best_for: Next.js and React projects wanting a polished Tailwind-based look with accessibility from React Aria.
entries.not_for: React only and tied to Tailwind v4. Migrating from NextUI or older HeroUI versions may involve API changes; smaller component set than MUI or Ant Design.

entries.name: json-render
entries.use_for: Let an AI generate UI as JSON limited to components you define, then render it in React, Vue, Svelte or React Native.
entries.why: Guardrailed output: the model can only use your catalog and your schema.
entries.summary: json-render is a generative UI framework. You define a catalog of components and actions with Zod schemas, the model returns a JSON spec within it, and a renderer streams it to the screen. It includes 36 shadcn/ui components and targets web, mobile, video and PDF.
entries.best_for: Apps where an LLM builds interfaces on the fly but must stay inside safe, known components.
entries.not_for: Free-form code generation of arbitrary UI. It only renders what your catalog allows.

entries.name: Kumo
entries.use_for: Build React apps with Cloudflare's accessible, design-system-compliant UI components.
entries.why: Built on Base UI, so keyboard navigation, focus management and ARIA are handled for you.
entries.summary: Kumo is Cloudflare's React component library. It builds on Base UI, re-exports the Base UI primitives, supports granular tree-shakable imports, and ships a CLI to query component docs. It also has a Figma plugin and a docs site.
entries.best_for: You build a React app and want accessible components in Cloudflare's design language.
entries.not_for: React only, and it needs react, react-dom and Phosphor icons as peer dependencies. Styled to Cloudflare's design system, so it is less neutral than a generic kit.

entries.name: Layui
entries.use_for: Classic web UI component library following native browser patterns
entries.why: No-build component kit popular for admin backends; plain HTML/JS usage without a framework.
entries.summary: Layui is an open source, MIT-licensed web UI component library built with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, without a framework. It aims to make building web interfaces easy for non-frontend developers. Layui 2 is current and Layui 3 is in development.
entries.best_for: Admin panels and internal web pages built without a frontend framework, especially by backend developers.
entries.not_for: React/Vue or modern SPA projects; the maintainers themselves recommend mainstream frameworks. Docs are mainly Chinese.

entries.name: Libraries.dev
entries.use_for: Add polished effects like border beams, thinking orbs and bot avatars to a React app.
entries.why: Seven standalone packages, each a single wrapper component tuned by props.
entries.summary: Seven React libraries for effects in AI interfaces: border beam, thinking orbs, bot avatars, gooey shapes, voice glow, liquid metal and an image loader. Each installs from npm and has zero runtime dependencies, except Image, which needs three.
entries.best_for: AI chat or agent UIs that need distinctive loading states and visual polish.
entries.not_for: Needs React 18+. A paid Pro plan unlocks the Studio and presets, so check the license before commercial use.

entries.name: Lucide
entries.use_for: Consistent open-source SVG icon set with packages for every framework
entries.why: Default icon set of shadcn/ui; 1,500+ icons, tree-shakable packages for React, Vue, Svelte and more.
entries.summary: Open-source icon library with 1600+ SVG icons and official packages for React, Vue, Svelte and other frameworks, plus plain SVG and web font options. Does not accept brand logos.
entries.best_for: Consistent line icons in React, Vue, Svelte or vanilla projects, including shadcn/ui setups.
entries.not_for: Does not include brand or logo icons and its single outline style is not suited if you need multiple weights or filled icon variants.

entries.name: M3E Canvas
entries.use_for: Sketch Material 3 Expressive app screens and turn the design into a prompt for an AI coding tool.
entries.why: Runs fully in the browser with no account, then outputs a build-ready brief.
entries.summary: A free, open-source sketchpad with real Material 3 Expressive parts. You drag parts onto phone or desktop screens, link screens to try the flow, set a theme, and copy a short prompt for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Cursor. Optional AI help uses your own key.
entries.best_for: Quickly planning an Android-style app UI before handing it to an AI coder.
entries.not_for: Production design handoff or non-Material designs. It outputs a prompt, not code or Figma files.

entries.name: Magic UI
entries.use_for: Animated copy-paste React components for landing pages, shadcn/ui compatible
entries.why: Most popular open animated-component collection in the shadcn ecosystem; installs through the shadcn CLI.
entries.summary: Collection of animated React components, shadcn/ui compatible, aimed at design engineers building landing pages. The README is minimal and points to magicui.design/docs.
entries.best_for: Landing pages and marketing sites that want ready-made animated effects installed via the shadcn CLI.
entries.not_for: Decorative marketing components, not a general UI kit for apps. React with Tailwind assumed; README gives little detail, so check the docs before adopting.

entries.name: Mantine
entries.use_for: Build React apps with a full-featured component library plus hooks, forms and notifications.
entries.why: Batteries included with 100+ components and 50+ hooks, good docs and easy theming without Tailwind.
entries.summary: React component library with 100+ components plus separate packages for hooks (80+), forms, charts, notifications, spotlight command palette, code highlight and a Tiptap rich-text editor.
entries.best_for: React apps wanting a batteries-included kit with forms, hooks and notifications and easy theming without Tailwind.
entries.not_for: React only. Ships its own styling system, so it pairs less naturally with Tailwind-first workflows than headless or copy-paste kits.

entries.name: Material UI
entries.use_for: Build React apps with a complete Material Design component library.
entries.why: The most adopted React component library, with a huge component set, theming and a commercial-grade data grid ecosystem.
entries.summary: Large React component library implementing Google's Material Design, extended by MUI X for advanced components. Long development history with extensive docs, examples and theming.
entries.best_for: React apps and dashboards that want a mature, widely adopted component set and Material Design look.
entries.not_for: React only and Material-styled by default, so heavy restyling is work. Advanced components (data grid, pickers) partly sit in MUI X, with commercial tiers.

entries.name: MudBlazor
entries.use_for: Build Blazor (.NET) web apps with Material-style components written in C#.
entries.why: The most popular Blazor component library, pure C# with minimal JavaScript.
entries.summary: Material Design component framework for Blazor written entirely in C#, designed so .NET developers can build web apps without writing much CSS or JavaScript. Has docs and an interactive playground.
entries.best_for: Blazor Server or WebAssembly apps in .NET that need a full Material-styled component set.
entries.not_for: Blazor/.NET only and Material-styled. Teams not using Blazor, or needing non-Material designs, should look elsewhere.

entries.name: Naive UI
entries.use_for: Complete Vue 3 component library with TypeScript and theming
entries.why: Around 90 components, fully typed, with CSS-in-JS theme overrides and no extra CSS import needed.
entries.summary: Vue 3 component library with 90+ TypeScript components, theme customization via overrides and no additional CSS import required.
entries.best_for: Vue 3 apps wanting a fairly complete, themeable, typed component set with a modern look.
entries.not_for: Vue 3 only and desktop-oriented. Community channels and docs are partly Chinese-oriented; ecosystem is smaller than Element Plus.

entries.name: Oat UI
entries.use_for: Style web apps with a tiny semantic HTML/CSS/JS component library that needs no build step.
entries.why: About 10KB, zero dependencies, styles plain semantic tags without class soup.
entries.summary: Oat is a UI library you use by including one CSS file and one JS file. Semantic tags and attributes are styled directly, and a few dynamic components are small Web Components. Demo and docs at oat.ink.
entries.best_for: Small projects, internal tools and server-rendered pages where you want decent looks with no framework or bundler.
entries.not_for: Large component ecosystems or React-style components. It is below v1 and the README warns of breaking changes.

entries.name: Open Intelligent UI
entries.use_for: Study or start from a generative UI app where an agent answers with text, native components or sandboxed custom UI.
entries.why: Shows an agent choosing between text, native components and streamed HTML/CSS/JS in an isolated iframe.
entries.summary: A CopilotKit reference app. A Python Deep Agent with focused skills streams to a Next.js frontend. Native components handle structured tasks, and generateSandboxedUi streams custom interactive HTML into a sandbox with a validated host bridge. An optional MCP server is included.
entries.best_for: Developers building chat apps where the agent should render charts, tables and small tools instead of only text.
entries.not_for: A drop-in component library. It is a full app with a Python agent and Next.js frontend, and sample data is only illustrative.

entries.name: OpenPencil
entries.use_for: Open and edit .fig design files, script them from a CLI, or build custom editors on a headless Vue SDK.
entries.why: Reads and writes native Figma files and exposes an MCP server and AI design tools.
entries.summary: An open-source design editor that opens `.fig` and `.pen` files and has built-in AI chat with 100+ tools that edit nodes. It ships a headless CLI, XPath queries, an MCP server, linting, token extraction and a headless Vue SDK.
entries.best_for: Automating or inspecting design files in code, or building your own design tool without Figma.
entries.not_for: The README says it is in active development with rough edges. Not a full replacement for every Figma feature.

entries.name: OpenPencil
entries.use_for: Generate and edit UI designs on a canvas from prompts, and export to React and Tailwind or HTML and CSS.
entries.why: Designs are plain JSON files that diff in Git, with a built-in MCP server and agent teams.
entries.summary: An open-source AI-native vector design tool. You describe a page and it is generated on the canvas, with agent teams working in parallel. Designs are saved as JSON `.op` files and can be exported as code.
entries.best_for: Teams who want an open, scriptable alternative to Figma-style tools with AI generation and MCP access.
entries.not_for: A design app, not a component library. Needs an AI model provider, and the project is young.

entries.name: Pretext
entries.use_for: Measure and lay out multiline text without DOM reads, then render to DOM, Canvas or SVG.
entries.why: Avoids layout reflow by using its own measurement logic, grounded in the browser font engine.
entries.summary: Pretext is a pure JS/TS library for fast multiline text measurement and layout across many languages. It skips getBoundingClientRect and offsetHeight, which cause reflow. You can render the result to the DOM, Canvas or SVG.
entries.best_for: You need accurate, fast text wrapping for canvas UIs, virtual lists or custom renderers.
entries.not_for: Not a full font rendering engine yet. It targets common CSS text setups and warns that system-ui fonts are unreliable on macOS.

entries.name: PrimeNG
entries.use_for: Large Angular UI component suite with themes
entries.why: One of the most complete Angular libraries: 90+ components including advanced data tables and charts.

license_verified.note: Community versions are MIT; -lts suffixed releases are under a separate commercial license

entries.summary: Large Angular UI suite with 90+ components including advanced tables and charts. The repo now carries a notice that it is no longer under active development and gets security fixes only; development moved to PrimeUI. Existing MIT releases stay MIT.
entries.best_for: Maintaining existing Angular apps already using PrimeNG, which stay on MIT releases with security fixes.
entries.not_for: Poor choice for new projects here: the repo is security-only and development continues under PrimeUI. Check licensing and the successor before adopting.

entries.name: PrimeReact
entries.use_for: Large React component suite with rich data tables, charts and form inputs
entries.why: Broadest prebuilt widget set for React enterprise/admin apps, themeable or unstyled with Tailwind.
entries.summary: Large React component suite with data tables, charts and form inputs, themeable or unstyled for Tailwind. The repo notice says it is no longer actively developed and receives security fixes only; work continues in PrimeUI.
entries.best_for: Existing React projects already built on PrimeReact that rely on its MIT releases and security patches.
entries.not_for: Not recommended for new projects from this repo: security-fix-only, with new features at PrimeUI. Read the migration notes first.

entries.name: PrimeVue
entries.use_for: 90+ Vue components incl. advanced DataTable, styled or unstyled (Tailwind) mode
entries.why: The most complete Vue component suite; strong data-heavy widgets beyond what Vuetify/Element Plus offer.
entries.summary: Vue UI suite with 90+ components including an advanced DataTable, offering styled and unstyled (Tailwind) modes. The README warns the repo is security-fixes-only and development continues at PrimeUI.
entries.best_for: Maintaining existing Vue apps built on PrimeVue's MIT releases.
entries.not_for: New projects should be careful: the repo is no longer actively developed and moved to PrimeUI. Consider current alternatives or the successor.

entries.name: Radix Primitives
entries.use_for: Build your own design system on unstyled, accessible React primitives.
entries.why: Handles focus, keyboard and ARIA correctly; the foundation under shadcn/ui and many design systems.
entries.summary: Low-level, unstyled React component library focused on accessibility, customization and developer experience. Usable as the base layer of a design system and adoptable incrementally.
entries.best_for: Building your own design system in React with correct focus, keyboard and ARIA handling; also the base under shadcn/ui.
entries.not_for: No styling and React only, so you write all visuals yourself. Not a ready-made kit for fast prototypes without something like shadcn/ui on top.

entries.name: React Spectrum / React Aria
entries.use_for: Build accessible custom components with React Aria hooks or use the Spectrum design system.
entries.why: Best-in-class accessibility and internationalization from Adobe; React Aria Components work with any styling.
entries.summary: Collection of libraries including React Aria hooks and components for accessible, adaptive, internationalized UI, plus the React Spectrum design system. Follows WAI-ARIA patterns with screen reader and keyboard support across devices.
entries.best_for: Accessibility-critical or internationalized React apps, or custom design systems built on React Aria with your own styling.
entries.not_for: React only. The Spectrum design system has a distinct Adobe look, and building from React Aria hooks takes more assembly work than a styled kit.

entries.name: Semi Design
entries.use_for: ByteDance React design system with themeable components
entries.why: Production design system from ByteDance with 70+ components, design-token theming and an a11y focus.
entries.summary: ByteDance's React design system and UI library with design-token theming, Figma resources and DesignOps tooling. Described as modern, comprehensive and flexible.
entries.best_for: React enterprise or content apps needing a themeable design system with Figma design tooling.
entries.not_for: React only with Douyin/ByteDance styling and a mainly Chinese-speaking community; smaller Western ecosystem than MUI or Ant Design.

entries.name: shadcn-vue
entries.use_for: Vue port of shadcn/ui: copy-in accessible components built on Reka UI and Tailwind
entries.why: The community standard for shadcn-style components in Vue/Nuxt; same CLI workflow as shadcn/ui.
entries.summary: Vue port of shadcn/ui: a set of components you copy into your project via CLI, built on Reka UI and Tailwind so you own and customize the code.
entries.best_for: Vue and Nuxt projects wanting shadcn-style editable, accessible components with Tailwind.
entries.not_for: Not an installable package with auto-updates; copied code is yours to maintain. Requires Tailwind and is Vue-only.

entries.name: shadcn/ui
entries.use_for: Copy accessible, Tailwind-styled React components into your project via a CLI.
entries.why: You own the code, built on Radix and Tailwind; the de-facto default for new React/Next.js apps and well known to coding agents.
entries.summary: Set of accessible components you copy into your project through a CLI, built on Radix and Tailwind. Code lives in your repo so you can customize it; it is meant as a base for your own component library.
entries.best_for: New React or Next.js projects using Tailwind that want editable components and a large community of examples.
entries.not_for: React and Tailwind only; no automatic upgrades since code is copied, and no data-heavy widgets such as advanced data grids out of the box.

entries.name: ShipSwift
entries.use_for: Give your AI assistant production-ready SwiftUI components and full-stack recipes to build iOS apps.
entries.why: Components and recipes are served to AI assistants over MCP, with a live searchable catalog.
entries.summary: An AI-native SwiftUI component library. The iOS client code is MIT licensed, and an MCP connection lets assistants pull components and recipes. Paid Pro recipes add backend routes, integration guides and compliance templates.
entries.best_for: Building an iOS app with an AI coding assistant that needs reliable SwiftUI building blocks.
entries.not_for: Backend code, guides and compliance templates are in paid Pro recipes. The open-source part is the iOS client code only.

entries.name: Stencil
entries.use_for: Compiler for building framework-agnostic web component design systems
entries.why: Powers Ionic: write components once in TSX and ship them as standard web components with React/Vue/Angular wrappers.
entries.summary: Compiler that generates standard Web Components from TypeScript and JSX class-style components, built by the Ionic team. Output works in any framework or none.
entries.best_for: Framework-agnostic design systems or component libraries that must be consumed from React, Angular, Vue and plain HTML.
entries.not_for: Not an app framework; adds a compiler step and its own conventions. For single-framework apps, native components in that framework are simpler.

entries.name: Storybook
entries.use_for: Build, document and test UI components in isolation
entries.why: Industry-standard workshop for design systems; works with React, Vue, Angular, Svelte and web components.
entries.summary: Frontend workshop for building, documenting and testing UI components and pages in isolation, with an addon system for design, docs and interaction testing. Supports React, Vue, Angular, Svelte and web components.
entries.best_for: Component libraries and design systems needing living documentation, visual review and isolated development.
entries.not_for: Not a component library itself; adds config and build overhead. Small apps with few shared components may not need it.

entries.name: Vuetify
entries.use_for: Build Vue apps with a Material Design component framework.
entries.why: Long-running, comprehensive Vue component framework with 1,000+ contributors and good accessibility.
entries.summary: Material Design component framework for Vue with hand-crafted components and a project scaffold command (create vuetify). Works with Nuxt or Laravel and has a large contributor base.
entries.best_for: Vue applications wanting a full Material Design look with many ready components.
entries.not_for: Vue only and Material-styled, so custom brand looks need effort. Not a headless or Tailwind-based option.
